stories.headline: OpenAI Closes Record $122B Funding Round at $852B Valuation, Reports $2B Monthly Revenue

key_facts.fact: OpenAI closed $122 billion in committed capital at an $852 billion post-money valuation, up from the $110 billion announced in February.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we closed our latest funding round with $122 billion in committed capital at a post money valuation of $852 billion.

key_facts.fact: The round was anchored by Amazon ($50B), NVIDIA ($30B), SoftBank ($30B), and Microsoft, with co-leads including a16z, D.E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, and TPG.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank co-led the round alongside other investors, including Andreessen Horowitz and D. E. Shaw Ventures, OpenAI said.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is now generating $2 billion in revenue per month, with enterprise accounting for more than 40% of revenue, on track to reach parity with consumer by end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: We are now generating $2B in revenue per month. Enterprise now makes up more than 40% of our revenue, and is on track to reach parity with consumer by the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT has over 900 million weekly active users and more than 50 million subscribers. Codex serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in three months.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT is the overwhelming leader in consumer AI with more than 900 million weekly active users, and over 50 million subscribers. Codex now serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in the past three months.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI extended participation to retail investors for the first time, raising over $3 billion through bank channels, and will be included in ARK Invest ETFs.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, we extended participation to investors through bank channels, raising over $3 billion from individual investors. Today, we're also announcing that OpenAI will be included in several exchange-traded funds managed by ARK Invest.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank took out a $40 billion bridge loan from major financial institutions to fund its OpenAI investment.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank Group recently took out a $40 billion bridge loan from a collection of big name financial institutions.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced plans to build a 'unified AI superapp' combining ChatGPT, Codex, browsing, and agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience.
key_facts.excerpt: That is why we are building a unified AI superapp. Users do not want disconnected tools. They want a single system that can understand intent, take action, and operate across applications, data, and workflows.

stories.headline: Anthropic Accidentally Leaks Claude Code's 512K-Line Source Code via Misconfigured npm Package

key_facts.fact: A 59.8 MB JavaScript source map file was inadvertently included in version 2.1.88 of the @anthropic-ai/claude-code npm package, exposing approximately 512,000 lines of TypeScript across ~1,900 files.
key_facts.excerpt: A 59.8 MB JavaScript source map file (.map), intended for internal debugging, was inadvertently included in version 2.1.88 of the @anthropic-ai/claude-code package on the public npm registry.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic confirmed the leak was 'a release packaging issue caused by human error, not a security breach' and said no sensitive customer data or credentials were exposed.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic leaked part of the internal source code for its popular artificial intelligence coding assistant, Claude Code, the company confirmed on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: The leaked source revealed internal codenames: Capybara (Mythos) for a Claude 4.6 variant already at v8, Fennec for Opus 4.6, and Numbat as an unreleased model still in testing.
key_facts.excerpt: The leak confirms that Capybara is the internal codename for a Claude 4.6 variant, with Fennec mapping to Opus 4.6 and the unreleased Numbat still in testing.

key_facts.fact: The code revealed a 'Self-Healing Memory' architecture, a three-layer memory system using lightweight pointers and on-demand topic files rather than traditional store-everything retrieval.
key_facts.excerpt: The leaked source reveals a sophisticated, three-layer memory architecture that moves away from traditional 'store-everything' retrieval.

key_facts.fact: The source revealed a KAIROS feature flag (mentioned 150+ times) for an autonomous daemon mode that allows Claude Code to operate as an always-on background agent performing memory consolidation.
key_facts.excerpt: KAIROS represents a fundamental shift in user experience: an autonomous daemon mode. While current AI tools are largely reactive, KAIROS allows Claude Code to operate as an always-on background agent.

key_facts.fact: Claude Code has achieved an annualized recurring revenue of $2.5 billion, more than doubling since the beginning of the year, with enterprise adoption accounting for 80% of its revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Market data indicates that Claude Code alone has achieved an annualized recurring revenue (ARR) of $2.5 billion, a figure that has more than doubled since the beginning of the year.

key_facts.fact: A clean-room Python reimplementation of the leaked code (claw-code) hit 44,500 GitHub stars within hours, raising questions about DMCA-proof derived works created by AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Gergely Orosz argued that the leaked TS source was rewritten in Python via OpenAI's Codex in hours, creating a DMCA-proof derived work that cannot be taken down. The claw-code repo hit 44,500 stars.

stories.headline: Google Warns Quantum Computers Could Break Crypto Encryption With 20x Fewer Qubits Than Expected

key_facts.fact: Google Quantum AI published a whitepaper showing elliptic curve cryptography protecting Bitcoin, Ethereum, and most cryptocurrencies could be broken with fewer than 500,000 physical qubits, down from roughly 9-10 million previously estimated — a 20-fold reduction.
key_facts.excerpt: They achieved this using fewer than 1,200 logical qubits and around 90 million Toffoli gate operations, which roughly represents a 20-fold reduction in the quantum resources previously thought necessary.

key_facts.fact: The attack could be executed in minutes on a sufficiently powerful quantum machine. Under idealized conditions, a primed quantum computer has a roughly 41% probability of deriving a private key before a Bitcoin transaction is confirmed.
key_facts.excerpt: Under idealized conditions, Google estimates a roughly 41% probability that a primed quantum computer could derive a private key before a Bitcoin transaction is confirmed.

key_facts.fact: In an unprecedented move, Google chose not to publish the actual circuits, instead releasing a zero-knowledge proof that lets researchers verify the claims without reproducing the attack. This was developed in coordination with the US government.
key_facts.excerpt: Google chose not to publish the actual quantum circuits behind their newest estimates, instead releasing a zero-knowledge proof: a cryptographic technique that lets independent researchers verify that the claims are mathematically sound.

key_facts.fact: The paper was co-authored with Justin Drake of the Ethereum Foundation and Dan Boneh of Stanford. It is the third major quantum threat paper in twelve months, following Gidney's RSA paper and Iceberg Quantum's Pinnacle architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Quantum AI published a whitepaper with co-authors including Justin Drake of the Ethereum Foundation and Dan Boneh of Stanford.

key_facts.fact: Google has set a 2029 internal deadline for its own post-quantum cryptography migration, a signal that carries particular weight given its own researchers produced these estimates.
key_facts.excerpt: The news comes just days after Google moved up its timeline for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography, setting a 2029 target after faster-than-expected advances in quantum computing.

stories.headline: OpenAI Ships Official Codex Plugin for Rival Anthropic's Claude Code

key_facts.fact: OpenAI open-sourced a plugin under Apache 2.0 that installs directly inside Anthropic's Claude Code, adding slash commands for code reviews, adversarial reviews, and task delegation to Codex.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI published a Codex plugin on March 30 that installs directly inside Anthropic's Claude Code, letting developers run code reviews and delegate tasks to Codex without leaving their existing workflow.

key_facts.fact: The plugin provides six slash commands including /codex:review for standard reviews, /codex:adversarial-review for challenge reviews questioning implementation decisions, and /codex:rescue for full task delegation.
key_facts.excerpt: /codex:review runs a standard read-only Codex code review. /codex:adversarial-review adds a steerable challenge mode. /codex:rescue hands work off to Codex entirely.

key_facts.fact: The move reflects competitive dynamics: Claude Code leads developer adoption with a $2.5B annualized run rate and 135,000 daily GitHub commits, while Codex has reached 1.6 million weekly active users.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Code contributed to a $2.5 billion annualized run rate for Anthropic and generates 135,000 daily commits on GitHub. Codex has reached 1.6 million weekly active users.

key_facts.fact: A same-day vulnerability disclosure revealed a critical command injection flaw in Codex via manipulated branch names, potentially exposing GitHub OAuth tokens. OpenAI patched the issue.
key_facts.excerpt: Phantom Labs disclosed a critical vulnerability in Codex itself. The flaw allowed command injection through manipulated branch names during task creation, potentially exposing GitHub OAuth tokens.

stories.headline: North Korean Hackers Compromise Axios npm Package in Supply Chain Attack Affecting Millions

key_facts.fact: Malicious versions of the axios npm package (1.14.1 and 0.30.4) were published via a hijacked maintainer account, injecting a remote access trojan targeting macOS, Windows, and Linux. The package has over 300 million weekly downloads.
key_facts.excerpt: A suspected North Korean hacker has hijacked and modified a popular open source software development tool to deliver malware that could put millions of developers at risk.

key_facts.fact: Google attributed the attack to UNC1069, a suspected North Korean financially-motivated threat actor that Google covered in a February blog post.
key_facts.excerpt: Hackers connected to North Korea are responsible for the recent compromise of a wildly popular library.

key_facts.fact: The malicious versions were live for approximately 2-4 hours before npm unpublished them. Cognition's Devin caught the attack for customers within one hour of injection.
key_facts.excerpt: Live for ~2-4 hours before npm unpublished them. Cognition's Devin Review caught the attack for customers within an hour.

key_facts.fact: The axios attack occurred hours before the Claude Code source leak, and the leaked Claude Code codebase itself was found to use the compromised axios package.
key_facts.excerpt: The most immediate danger is a concurrent, separate supply-chain attack on the axios npm package, which occurred hours before the leak.

stories.headline: Google Launches Veo 3.1 Lite, Cuts AI Video Generation Costs by 50% as OpenAI Exits Sora

key_facts.fact: Google launched Veo 3.1 Lite, a cost-effective video generation model at less than 50% the cost of Veo 3.1 Fast, supporting both text-to-video and image-to-video at 720p or 1080p.
key_facts.excerpt: Veo 3.1 Lite slots under Veo 3.1 Fast, with Veo 3.1 remaining at the top. This new offering is Google's 'most cost-effective video model.' It is 'less than 50% of the cost of Veo 3.1 Fast.'

key_facts.fact: The model supports landscape (16:9) and portrait (9:16) aspect ratios with customizable duration at 4, 6, or 8 seconds. It is available today via the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
key_facts.excerpt: Developers can also customize duration at 4s, 6s, or 8s, with cost adjusting accordingly. Veo 3.1 Lite is rolling out today on the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

key_facts.fact: The launch came following OpenAI's shutdown of its Sora video generation tool the previous week, with Google explicitly affirming its commitment to video generation tools.
key_facts.excerpt: Following OpenAI's Sora exit last week, Google today said it's committed to offering video generation while announcing Veo 3.1 Lite.

stories.headline: AI Recruiting Startup Mercor Confirms Breach via LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack, Lapsus$ Claims 4TB Stolen

key_facts.fact: Mercor confirmed it was 'one of thousands of companies' affected by a supply chain attack on the open-source LiteLLM project, linked to hacking group TeamPCP.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI startup told TechCrunch on Tuesday that it was 'one of thousands of companies' affected by a recent compromise of LiteLLM's project, which was linked to a hacking group called TeamPCP.

key_facts.fact: Extortion group Lapsus$ claimed responsibility and shared samples including Slack data, ticketing data, and videos of conversations between Mercor's AI systems and contractors. They claim 939GB of source code and 4TB total data.
key_facts.excerpt: Lapsus$ claimed responsibility for the apparent data breach on its leak site and shared a sample of data allegedly taken from Mercor, which TechCrunch reviewed.

key_facts.fact: Mercor was valued at $10 billion following a $350 million Series C in October 2025 and works with OpenAI and Anthropic to train AI models by contracting domain experts.
key_facts.excerpt: Mercor works with companies including OpenAI and Anthropic to train AI models. The startup was valued at $10 billion following a $350 million Series C round led by Felicis Ventures in October 2025.

key_facts.fact: The LiteLLM compromise involved malicious code in packages discovered last week; the library is downloaded millions of times per day according to security firm Snyk.
key_facts.excerpt: The compromise of LiteLLM originally surfaced last week after malicious code was discovered in a package associated with the Y Combinator-backed startup's open-source project.

stories.headline: PrismML Emerges From Stealth With 1-Bit LLM That Fits 8B Parameters in 1.15GB, Runs on iPhone

key_facts.fact: PrismML, a Caltech-origin AI lab, emerged from stealth with $16.25M in SAFE and seed funding, claiming its 1-bit Bonsai 8B model achieves radical compression without sacrificing performance.
key_facts.excerpt: PrismML launched 1-bit Bonsai, an 8B-parameter model squeezed into 1.15 GB (14x smaller than peers) that runs on an iPhone at 40 tokens/sec.

key_facts.fact: Bonsai 8B is a true end-to-end 1-bit model (embeddings, attention, MLP, and LM head all 1-bit) with 10.6x intelligence density per GB over Qwen3 8B, running at 40 tok/s on iPhone, 136 tok/s on M4 Pro, and 440 tok/s on RTX 4090.
key_facts.excerpt: A true end-to-end 1-bit model with 10.6x intelligence density over Qwen3 8B. Runs at 136 tok/s on M4 Pro and 440 tok/s on RTX 4090.

key_facts.fact: PrismML claims 1-bit Bonsai 8B scores 1.06 intelligence per GB compared to 0.10/GB for the closest full-precision 8B model, representing a 10x improvement in intelligence density.
key_facts.excerpt: Intelligence density = how much useful intelligence a model delivers per GB. By this measure, 1-bit Bonsai 8B scores 1.06/GB, while the closest nearby full-precision 8B model scores 0.10/GB.

stories.headline: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-350M, a 350M-Parameter Model Trained on 28T Tokens for Edge Agentic Tasks

key_facts.fact: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-350M, a 350-million parameter model trained on 28 trillion tokens (80,000:1 token-to-parameter ratio), using a hybrid architecture of Linear Input-Varying Systems and Grouped Query Attention.
key_facts.excerpt: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-350M with additional pre-training from 10T to 28T tokens and large-scale reinforcement learning.

key_facts.fact: The model supports a 32K context window while running on extremely limited hardware: 169MB on Snapdragon NPU, 81MB on Snapdragon GPU, and 300MB on Raspberry Pi 5. On an H100, it reaches 40.4K output tokens per second.
key_facts.excerpt: Snapdragon 8 Elite NPU: 169MB peak memory. Snapdragon GPU: 81MB peak memory. Raspberry Pi 5: 300MB. On a single NVIDIA H100 GPU, the model can reach a throughput of 40.4K output tokens per second.

key_facts.fact: The model scores 76.96 on IFEval (instruction following) and is optimized for tool use, function calling, and structured data extraction, though explicitly not recommended for complex coding or creative writing.
key_facts.excerpt: The high IFEval score indicates the model is efficient at following complex, structured instructions, making it suitable for tool use, function calling, and structured data extraction.

stories.headline: Hugging Face Releases TRL v1.0, Stable Post-Training Library With Async GRPO and Tool-Calling Support

key_facts.fact: Hugging Face released TRL v1.0, transitioning the post-training library from a research codebase into stable infrastructure for foundation model training, now handling approximately a significant portion of open-source RL training.
key_facts.excerpt: TRL v1.0: Post-Training Library Built to Move with the Field. Published March 31, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Key additions include Asynchronous GRPO (parallel rollouts eliminating idle GPU time), new RL trainers (VESPO, DPPO, SDPO), tool-calling support, and full OpenEnv integration for stateful multi-turn environment training.
key_facts.excerpt: Hugging Face released TRL v1.0, the post-training library now built as stable infrastructure with Asynchronous GRPO, new RL trainers (VESPO, DPPO, SDPO), tool-calling support, and full OpenEnv integration.

key_facts.fact: The release enables developers to do the first successful GRPO fine-tune of models on live environments — demonstrated with Qwen3-1.7B on TextArena Wordle, taking win rate from 0% to 8%.
key_facts.excerpt: arora_mrinaal demoed the first successful GRPO fine-tune of Qwen3-1.7B on live TextArena Wordle via TRL + OpenEnv, taking win rate from 0% to 8%.

stories.headline: Yupp AI Shuts Down Less Than a Year After $33M Seed Led by a16z Crypto

key_facts.fact: Yupp, a crowdsourced AI model-picking service backed by $33M from a16z crypto's Chris Dixon, announced it is shutting down less than a year after launch, saying it 'didn't reach a strong enough product-market fit.'
key_facts.excerpt: Less than a year after launching, Yupp is closing its business. It 'didn't reach a strong enough product-market fit' to survive, in part because AI models improved by such leaps and bounds these past few months.

key_facts.fact: Yupp had signed up 1.3 million users and allowed consumers to test and compare results from 800 AI models for free, generating crowdsourced preference data that AI labs would pay for.
key_facts.excerpt: Yupp said it signed up 1.3 million users and collected millions of preferences every month.

key_facts.fact: The founders cited rapid AI model improvements as a key factor, noting the industry shifted to hiring specialty experts (PhDs) for reinforcement learning feedback rather than crowdsourced consumer data.
key_facts.excerpt: While labs are paying big bucks for feedback, the current model — pioneered by companies like Scale AI and Mercor — is to hire specialty experts, like PhDs, and tuck them into the reinforcement learning loop.

stories.headline: Baidu Robotaxi Fleet Freezes Across Wuhan in System Failure, Trapping Passengers on Highways

key_facts.fact: A suspected system failure caused dozens of Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis to freeze simultaneously across Wuhan, China on Tuesday, trapping passengers in vehicles and reportedly causing traffic disruptions and crashes on highways.
key_facts.excerpt: An unknown technical problem caused a number of robotaxis owned by the Chinese tech giant Baidu to freeze on Tuesday in the middle of traffic, trapping passengers.

key_facts.fact: Some passengers were trapped for more than an hour, with one telling Wired it took 30 minutes to exit the vehicle. Wuhan traffic police said it was 'likely caused by a system malfunction' but still under investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu robotaxi outage in Wuhan caused by 'system failure', police say.

key_facts.fact: The incident occurred the same day Baidu Apollo Go and WeRide started driverless commercial operations in Dubai, highlighting the contrast between expansion ambitions and reliability concerns.
